question: Above what turnover must a supplier issue an e-invoice with an IRN?
gold: Aggregate annual turnover above ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: Above ₹5 crore aggregate annual turnover
Answer: A supplier whose aggregate annual turnover (AATO) in any financial year since 2017-18 has exceeded ₹5 crore must issue an e-invoice with an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code. [1] If such a supplier sends an invoice without an IRN, the invoice is not valid for input tax credit and is returned with the exception code IRN_MISSING. [1][2] The base value of an invoice missing an IRN must not be paid; a valid e-invoice will follow. [1]

question: How is a duplicate invoice detected?
gold: Same supplier GSTIN and normalised invoice number (spaces, slashes, hyphens, leading zeros and /A, /R or -REV suffixes removed), or same supplier, invoice date and total within ₹1.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Answer: A duplicate invoice is detected by comparing each invoice against invoices received in the last 18 months for the same supplier using a normalised invoice number. [1] The system normalises the invoice number by removing spaces, slashes, hyphens, leading zeros, and trailing suffixes /A, /R, or -REV before comparison. [1] Two invoices are flagged as suspected duplicates when the supplier GSTIN and normalised invoice number match, or when the supplier, invoice date, and total amount (within ₹1) match. [1] Suspected duplicates are routed to the exception queue with code DUP_SUSPECT and are blocked from posting until a Senior Processor clears them. [1]
Expert tip: Duplicate invoices must be sent to DUP_SUSPECT with a note and not overridden.
Older sources (superseded): reject the new invoice as a duplicate (AP SOP v3.1 §2); stop and raise DUP_SUSPECT; do not override (DI-03 Part A, step 2); stop_and_raise_DUP_SUSPECT (Video 1 [02:10])
